title: Simplicial sets, nondegenerate simplices, simplicial subsets
statement: Let $\Delta$ be the category whose objects are the finite totally ordered sets $[n]=\{0<1<\dots<n\}$, $n\geq0$, and whose morphisms are the order-preserving maps. A *simplicial set* $S$ is a functor $S:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$; $S_n=S([n])$ is its set of *$n$-simplices*, and for $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$ the map $S(\varphi):S_n\to S_m$ is the *simplicial operator* of $\varphi$ (the face maps $d_i=S(\delta_i)$, $\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]$ the injection omitting $i$, and the degeneracy maps $s_i=S(\sigma_i)$, $\sigma_i:[n+1]\to[n]$ the surjection repeating $i$). A morphism of simplicial sets is a natural transformation. An $n$-simplex $x\in S_n$ is *degenerate* if $x=S(f)(y)$ for some order-preserving $f:[n]\to[m]$ with $m<n$ and some $y\in S_m$, and *nondegenerate* otherwise. A *simplicial subset* $U\subseteq S$ is a family of subsets $U_n\subseteq S_n$ with $S(\varphi)(U_n)\subseteq U_m$ for every $\varphi:[m]\to[n]$; with the restricted operators it is a simplicial set. $S$ *has finitely many nondegenerate simplices* if the set $\coprod_{n\geq0}\{x\in S_n: x\text{ nondegenerate}\}$ is finite.
